neighbours.label: a preposition after a tally or trend where 'the last / past / first N <periods>' is expected next (over, in, for, during)
fire: Rents in the capital have climbed steadily over the past five years.
The striker has netted nine goals in his last eleven matches.
The firm has reported losses for each of the last three quarters.
Average rainfall has dropped by a third over the last two decades.
He lost eight pounds in the first four weeks of the diet.
The club has won three league titles over the past ten seasons.
Unemployment has fallen in each of the past six months.
Membership grew by forty percent during the last two years.
quiet: Rents in the capital are paid on the first day of the month.
The striker wears the number nine shirt and lives near the stadium.
The firm moved its headquarters to a tower by the river.
Average rainfall is highest on the western side of the hills.
He bought new running shoes and a water bottle for the race.
The club plays its home games at an old stadium by the sea.
Unemployment offices open at nine and close at five.
Membership cards are printed on recycled paper.

notes: card: ' over' x9, ' in' x8 before 'the past three seasons', 'the first 6 weeks'; output promotes last/first/next. Probe: 'doubled over the past' 0.43; 'goals in' 0.18 whether or not 'the last' followed (causal), so near misses vary the lead-in, not just the next word.
